A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSFLOW research. All 24 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark rewards and training times, disease-testing results, and ablations in Table 1, Figures 3–4 and Section 5.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-instance scheduling and solver-backend experiments in Appendix M.

M1.justification: The spherical flow policy, solver mapping, weighted training objective, latent critic, smoothed Bellman operator and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new theoretical discussion and solver comparisons do not introduce a different proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four public benchmark tasks and four ICPSR disease networks. Appendix M varies scheduling instance sizes and solver backends within existing tasks; it does not add a distinct dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, but Appendix I.2 in v1 becomes J.2 in v2 and replaces the routing-cycle descriptions of Dynamic Assignment Random/Greedy with capacity-respecting assignment procedures. This revises the reported baseline definitions; unchanged Table 1 scores do not establish that implementations changed or experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds scheduling evaluations at patient/budget sizes 100/20, 200/30, 500/50 and 1000/80, plus a controlled Gurobi/SCIP/CPLEX comparison on Dynamic Intervention. Previously reported training settings, hyperparameter tables and evaluation-episode counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M adds focused tests of performance as scheduling instances grow and sensitivity to solver backend. Existing geometry, smoothing and critic-space ablations remain. Section 6 also newly reports qualitative instability in preliminary attempts to maximize critic values through the flow sampler.

E5.justification: New Table 5 explicitly identifies uncertainty as standard deviations over evaluation episodes, whereas v1's numerical spreads are unlabeled. Existing episode counts remain unchanged, with no added seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Changed Figure 3 band values are result changes, not evidence of a different uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix M adds scheduling results, including 218.77±2.97 for LSFLOW versus 204.07±1.49 for SRL at 1000/80, and SCIP/CPLEX rewards of 17.03±0.59 and 17.34±0.47. Figure 3 revises Gonorrhea Random, several HIV curves and Chlamydia SRL. Table 1 and Figure 4 remain unchanged; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: New Theorem 3.6 and Appendix H prove convergence of the smoothed fixed point to the unsmoothed value as concentration increases, assuming zero policy mass on solver-switching boundaries. Remark 3.7 explains why uniform convergence generally fails. Appendix G additionally extends contraction and smoothness guarantees to feasible measurable approximate solvers.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and principal conclusion retain the same claims about expressive feasible policies, efficient latent-space learning and improved performance, including the 20.6% average advantage. New theory and experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 more explicitly distinguishes finite-concentration smoothing bias from asymptotic consistency and states convergence limitations. Appendix G explains the changed value interpretation with approximate solvers. Section 6 adds direct-optimization instability and explicitly discusses inference-time solver overhead; the original Appendix A limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise to release code upon acceptance with a code-repository link. It also corrects Dynamic Assignment heuristic descriptions and names the three tested solver backends. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, preprocessing and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Zhang et al.'s energy-weighted flow matching and narrows its stated extension to online combinatorial RL in latent cost space. It also adds Kangaslahti et al. on networked testing and Khalil et al./Li et al. on learned solver guidance. Other bibliography edits largely correct metadata.

P1.justification: Localized explanations expand Sections 3.1 and 3.3, and Section 6 gains a limitations paragraph while Appendix A is retained. Acknowledgments, terminology and bibliographic wording are corrected. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, redraws Figure 3 with revised curves, relocates Figure 4 and several appendix displays, and changes conference formatting and spacing. The other original figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The consistency theorem strengthens the justification for smoothing, while targeted scalability and solver tests add practical support. Corrected baseline descriptions, clearer limitations and a code link improve clarity and reproducibility. These strengthen the retained contribution, although Figure 3's revisions are unexplained and the additional experiments provide limited procedural detail.
